It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 **Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py ` scans every `core.action.script` body and every `=js:` expression for the unsupported constructs listed above, plus the script-node rules (top-level `return` of an object, no `function main()` wrapper, no `console.log`, no `aggregate` variable). None of these are caught by `uip maestro flow validate`. 542 543 --- 544 545 ## Scoping Rules 546 547 ### Node Output Availability 548 549 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 550 551 ### Loop Scope 552 553 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 554 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 555 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 556 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 557 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 558 559 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 560 561 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 562 563 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 564 565 ### Subflow Scope 566 567 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 568 569 --- 570 571 ## Variable Management via CLI 572 573 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 574 575 ### Adding a workflow input variable 576 577 1. Open `.flow` 578 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 579 3. Run `uip maestro flow validate` to check for errors 580 581 ### Adding node variables after manual node insertion 582 583 When adding nodes via `Edit` (not CLI), you must also add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`: 584 585 ```json 586 { 587 "id": "myScript.output", 588 "type": "object", 589 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "output" } 590 }, 591 { 592 "id": "myScript.error", 593 "type": "object", 594 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "error" } 595 } 596 ``` 597 598 > **When using `uip maestro flow node add`**, node variables are handled automatically. Only add them manually when using `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 599 600 ### Mapping outputs on End nodes 601 602 For every `out` variable, add a mapping in each End node's `outputs`: 603 604 ```json 605 "outputs": { 606 "result": { 607 "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output" 608 } 609 } 610 ``` 611 612 --- 613 614 ## Complete Example 615 616 A flow with input, state, and output 1	# CLI Conventions
2	
3	Shared conventions for the `uip` CLI that apply across **all three capabilities** (Author, Operate, Diagnose). Read this first when invoking any `uip` command — every capability assumes these mechanics.
4	
5	## 1. Resolve the `uip` binary and detect command prefix
6	
7	The `uip` CLI is installed via npm. Resolve the binary (it may not be on PATH in nvm environments) and detect the command namespace.
8	
9	```bash
10	UIP=$(command -v uip 2>/dev/null || echo "$(npm root -g 2>/dev/null | sed 's|/node_modules$||')/bin/uip")
11	CURRENT=$($UIP --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $NF}')
12	```
13	
14	If `uip` is not found at all, install it:
15	
16	```bash
17	npm install -g @uipath/cli@latest
18	```
19	
20	If `npm install -g` fails with a permission error, prompt the user to re-run with appropriate privileges — do not retry automatically.
21	
22	### Command prefix by version
23	
24	| Installed version | Command prefix | Example |
25	| --- | --- | --- |
26	| **≥ 0.3.4** | `uip maestro flow` | `uip maestro flow init MyProject` |
27	| **< 0.3.4** | `uip flow` | `uip flow init MyProject` <!-- uip-check-skip --> |
28	
29	```bash
30	MIN_VERSION="0.3.4"
31	if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$MIN_VERSION" "$CURRENT" | sort -V | head -n1)" = "$MIN_VERSION" ]; then
32	  FLOW_CMD="uip maestro flow"
33	else
34	  FLOW_CMD="uip flow" # <!-- uip-check-skip -->  legacy < 0.3.4 prefix
35	fi
36	echo "Using: $FLOW_CMD (CLI version $CURRENT)"
37	```
38	
39	> **All commands across this skill are written as `uip maestro flow ...` (the ≥ 0.3.4 form).** If version detection above returns < 0.3.4, replace `uip maestro flow` with `uip flow`. Arguments and flags are identical — only the prefix differs. See UiPath/cli#841 for background on the restructuring. <!-- uip-check-skip -->

41	## 2. Always use `--output json`
42	
43	All `uip` commands support structured JSON output. Use `--output json` whenever output is parsed programmatically — every reference doc and recipe in this skill assumes it.
44	
45	```bash
46	uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json
47	uip maestro flow registry list --output json
48	uip maestro flow instance incidents <INSTANCE_ID> --folder-key <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
49	```
50	
51	> **Anti-pattern: `--format json` does NOT exist.** The flag is `--output json`. Using `--format json` produces `error: unknown option '--format'` and exit code 3 on every `uip` subcommand — not a helpful message pointing at `--output`.
52	
53	The `--localstorage-file` warning that appears in some environments is benign and can be ignored.
54	
55	## 3. Prefer `--output-filter` for extraction
56	
57	When extracting one field or a projection from `uip --output json`, use `--output-filter '<jmespath>'`. The CLI exposes `--output-filter <expression>` as a global flag on every subcommand; it applies a [JMESPath](https://jmespath.org/) expression to the `Data` envelope **before** printing. Write expressions starting at `Data` — do **not** prefix them with `Data.`.
58	
59	**Canonical example (broad discovery)** — list all nodes matching a keyword with the standard projection:
60	
61	```bash
62	uip maestro flow registry search slack --output json \
63	  --output-filter "[*].{NodeType:NodeType,DisplayName:DisplayName,Description:Description,AvailableOnTenant:AvailableOnTenant}"
64	```
65	
66	This is the form used in the connector skill — see [Cross-references](#cross-references) below — and is the right starting point when you want to inspect what's available.
67	
68	**Narrow query** — once you know the connector namespace, filter to a single connector's activities:
69	
70	```bash
71	uip maestro flow registry search slack --output json \
72	  --output-filter "[?starts_with(NodeType,'uipath.connector.uipath-salesforce-slack.')].{NodeType:NodeType,DisplayName:DisplayName}"
73	```
74	
75	`registry search` returns `Data` as a **flat array of PascalCase objects** — `NodeType`, `Category`, `DisplayName`, `Description`, `Version`, `Tags`, `AvailableOnTenant`. Not `Data.Nodes`, not lowercase `type`/`category`; those shapes do not exist. Knowing the shape lets you write the right expression on call #1 — which is the actual protection. Do **not** rely on `--output-filter` to *catch* a wrong-shape guess: a syntactically valid expression that simply doesn't match (e.g. `--output-filter "Nodes"` or `"Nodes[*].NodeType"` against the flat array) returns `Data: []` with **exit 0** — the same silent trap as `python3`/`jq` (see the silent-`[]` note below). Only an *invalid* expression fails loudly with exit 3: a syntax error, or a type error such as `keys(@)` on an array.
76	
77	> **Never `head`/`tail`/`grep -m`/pager a discovery query** (`registry search`, `is connectors list`, any `list`/`search`). A row past the cutoff reads exactly like a row that doesn't exist — the same false-absence trap as the silent `[]`, self-inflicted. To check existence, push the predicate into `--output-filter` so the result is *all* matches and already small; cap rows only on data already known complete or already filtered.
78	>
79	> ```bash
80	> uip … registry search slack --output json --output-filter "[?contains(NodeType,'get-channel-info')].NodeType"   # right: every match
81	> uip … registry search slack --output json --output-filter "[*].{…}" | head -100                                # wrong: hides matches past line 100
82	> ```
83	
84	### When to fall back to `python3` / `jq`
85	
86	`--output-filter` is the preferred extraction mechanism, but it is not a general-purpose transformation tool. Fall back to `python3 -c` or `jq` when JMESPath cannot express the operation:
87	
88	- Multi-step joins across two CLI calls.
89	- Format conversion (JSON → CSV, JSON → env-var assignments).
90	- Conditional output that depends on a value computed from multiple fields.
91	
92	Before reaching for an external parser, verify the JSON shape. The CLI roots `--output-filter` expressions at `Data`, so:
93	
94	- **Check whether `Data` is array or object first** — `--output-filter "type(@)"` returns `"array"` or `"object"`. `keys(@)` throws on arrays (`Filter 'keys(@)' failed to evaluate: Invalid type: keys() expected argument 1 to be type (object) but received type array instead`), so use `type(@)` as the first probe.
95	- **If `type(@)` returned `"object"`:** `--output-filter "keys(@)"` lists the top-level field names at `Data`.
96	- **If `type(@)` returned `"array"`:** `--output-filter "[0]"` shows the first row, or `--output-filter "[0] | keys(@)"` lists the keys of one row.
97	- **Watch for silent `[]`** — when the JMESPath path doesn't match anything, the CLI returns `Data: []` with `Result: "Success"`. That's the exact silent-failure mode the docs are designed to surface. If you got `Data: []` and were expecting a value, double-check field-name casing — **and note casing differs by command:**
98	  - `registry search` / `list` (and most `uip … --output json` commands) return **PascalCase** keys → filter `[*].NodeType`, `[*].DisplayName`.
99	  - `registry get` returns the node definition **verbatim** (it is pasted straight into the `.flow`), so its keys keep the manifest's own casing — predominantly **camelCase**: `Node.nodeType`, `Node.inputDefinition`, `Node.supportsErrorHandling`, `Node.form.sections[…]`. A few nested *runtime-output* schemas are PascalCase because the engine emits them that way (e.g. Summarize's `content.Text` / `content.Citations`) — match whatever the manifest actually declares, not a normalized form.
100	  - When unsure, probe before guessing: `--output-filter "keys(@)"` (object) or `--output-filter "[0] | keys(@)"` (array).
101	
102	Most agent-side retry loops on `uip --output json` parsing come from guessing the shape wrong; verify, then parse.
103	
104	### Cross-references
105	
106	The broad-discovery recipe above is used in [author/references/plugins/connector/planning.md](../author/references/plugins/connector/planning.md) (§ Discovery) for connector discovery and [author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for connection-resource lookup. Keep the three in sync on the **preference** (always `--output-filter`) and the **shape pin** (`registry search` Data is a flat array of PascalCase objects); each file may pick a projection appropriate to its task.
107	
108	## 4. CLI output JSON shape
109	
110	Every `uip` command returns one of two response shapes:
111	
112	**Success:**
113	```json
114	{ "Result": "Success", "Code": "FlowValidate", "Data": { ... } }
115	```
116	
117	**Failure:**
118	```json
119	{ "Result": "Failure", "Message": "...", "Instructions": "Found N error(s): ..." }
120	```
121	
122	Always check `Result` first. On failure, `Message` and `Instructions` carry the diagnostic detail.
123	
124	## 5. Login state
125	
126	| Capability | Login required? |
127	|---|---|
128	<!--skill-flavor:flow-init-login-scope:start-->
129	| **Author** | No — `flow init`, `validate`, `format`, registry (OOTB nodes), `Edit` / `Write` edits, planning all work offline |
130	<!--skill-flavor:flow-init-login-scope:end-->
131	| **Operate** | **Yes** — `solution upload`, `solution resources refresh`, `flow debug`, `flow pack`, `process run`, `job status`, `job traces` all require `uip login` |
132	| **Diagnose** | **Yes** — `instance incidents`, `instance variables`, `instance asset`, `incident get`, `incident summary` all require `uip login` |
133	
134	Tenant-specific connector and resource nodes in the registry also require login. Without login, registry shows OOTB nodes only. **In-solution sibling projects** are always available via `--local` without login.
135	
136	Check login status:
137	
138	```bash
139	uip login status --output json
140	```
141	
142	Log in interactively (opens browser):
143	
144	```bash
145	uip login
146	uip login --authority https://alpha.uipath.com    # non-production environments
147	```
148	
149	## 6. `--folder-key` requirement
150	
151	All `uip maestro flow instance` and `uip maestro flow incident get` commands require `--folder-key <FOLDER_KEY>` (`-f` shorthand). Without it, the command rejects the request before reaching the API.
152	
153	Get the folder key:
154	
155	```bash
156	uip or folders list --output json
157	```
158	
159	Or pull it from the job/process context (e.g., `Data.folderKey` on a job status response, or from the debug output's surrounding metadata).
160	
161	## 7. `UIPCLI_LOG_LEVEL=info` for debug runs
162	
163	Set `UIPCLI_LOG_LEVEL=info` on `flow debug` invocations to surface progress and diagnostic detail in the CLI output. Without it, debug runs return only the final result.
164	
165	```bash
166	UIPCLI_LOG_LEVEL=info uip maestro flow debug <path-to-project-dir> --output json
167	```
168	
169	The env var has no effect on other subcommands.
170	
171	## 8. Global options
172	
173	All `uip` commands support `--output json|yaml|table` and `--help`. Run any command with `--help` to discover all available options for that subcommand.
174	
175	```bash
176	uip maestro flow <subcommand> --help
177	```

commands.result_summary: /.uipath/.skills/skills/uipath-agents/references/lowcode/model-selection-guide.md

1	# Model Selection Guide
2	
3	How to pick the LLM for a low-code agent's `settings.model`. The tenant is the source of truth — discover at runtime, then select; never ship the scaffold default.
4	
5	> `uip agent init` for an autonomous agent scaffolds `settings.model: "gpt-5.4"` with a 128000 output cap. **Always override it** with a discovered current model before validating.
6	
7	> `uip agent init --conversational` for a conversational agent scaffolds `settings.model: "anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0"` with a 64000 output cap. It serves as a solid default but can be overwritten with a discovered current model before validating. 
8	
9	## 1. Discover (primary path)
10	
11	List the models the authenticated tenant actually offers:
12	
13	```bash
14	uip agent model list --output json
15	```
16	
17	`Data` is a **flat array of PascalCase objects** — not nested, not lowercase:
18	
19	| Field | Meaning |
20	|-------|---------|
21	| `Provider` | `OpenAi` \| `AwsBedrock` \| `VertexAi` |
22	| `Name` | The exact string for `settings.model` (e.g. `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, `gpt-5.4`) |
23	| `IsByo` | `true` = bring-your-own key registered for this tenant |
24	| `IsPreview` | `true` = preview/non-GA — avoid by default |
25	| `MaxTokens` | Output-token ceiling for this model — caps `settings.maxTokens` |
26	
27	Filter to selectable GA models with `--output-filter` (a global flag applied to `Data` — write the JMESPath starting at `Data`, no `Data.` prefix):
28	
29	```bash
30	uip agent model list --output json \
31	  --output-filter "[?IsByo==\`false\` && IsPreview==\`false\`].{Name:Name,Provider:Provider,MaxTokens:MaxTokens}"
32	```
33	
34	Run discovery **before** choosing a model. Do not pick from this doc's examples without confirming the name appears in the live list — model availability differs per tenant and changes over time.
35	
36	## 2. Select
37	
38	1. Start from the GA-filtered list above (`IsByo=false`, `IsPreview=false`).
39	2. **Preview models are opt-in only.** Use an `IsPreview: true` model (e.g. `gpt-5.5-2026-04-23`, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`) **only when the user explicitly asks** for the bleeding edge — preview models can change behavior or availability without notice.
40	3. Pick the **newest GA model matching the task class** (§3).
41	4. Set `settings.maxTokens` from the chosen model's `MaxTokens` — never exceed the cap. Example: `gpt-4o-2024-11-20` caps at 16384, so `maxTokens: 32768` is invalid for it; `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` caps at 64000; `gpt-5.4` at 128000.
42	
43	## 3. Task → model mapping
44	
45	Express the choice as **selection criteria over the discovered list**, not a fixed ID:
46	
47	| Task class | Selection criterion | Why |
48	|------------|---------------------|-----|
49	| Reasoning / judgment / multi-step tool use | Newest GA Anthropic Sonnet or Opus, or newest GA flagship OpenAI | Strongest instruction-following + tool-call discipline |
50	| Fast / cheap / high-volume classification or extraction | Newest GA `*-mini` (e.g. an OpenAI `*-mini`) or GA Haiku | Lower latency + cost; sufficient for narrow deterministic tasks |
51	| Long-context (large documents, big tool outputs) | GA model with the highest `MaxTokens` | Avoids truncated output |
52	| Conversational | Newest GA Anthropic Sonnet or user preference | Strongest conversational responses and instruction-following |
53	
54	Concrete GA examples observed on a live tenant — **illustrative only; verify against `uip agent model list`**:
55	
56	- Reasoning: `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, `anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14`
57	- Fast/cheap: `gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17`, `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`, `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`
58	
59	## 4. Fallback (discovery unavailable)
60	
61	If `uip agent model list` fails (not logged in, offline, command unavailable), pick a curated GA default — currently `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` for reasoning tasks — and **tell the user it was not tenant-verified** and may not exist on their tenant. This is the only situation where a hardcoded name is the operative choice; everywhere else, discover first.
62	
63	## 5. Apply the choice
64	
65	Edit `settings.model` (and `settings.maxTokens`) in `agent.json`, then refresh and validate:
66	
67	1. Set `settings.model` to the discovered `Name`.
68	2. Set `settings.maxTokens` ≤ the model's `MaxTokens`.
69	3. `uip agent refresh --output json`
70	4. `uip agent validate --output json`
71	
72	For inline-in-flow agents add `--inline-in-flow` to both commands. Full field reference: [agent-definition.md](agent-definition.md#change-model-settings).
73

1	# Inline Agent in a Flow
2	
3	Walkthrough for embedding a low-code autonomous agent directly inside a flow project. The agent lives as a UUID-named subdirectory inside the flow project and is published with the parent flow.
4	
5	Flow authoring itself is the responsibility of the `uipath-maestro-flow` skill — this file covers only the inline-agent side (creating the agent subdirectory, configuring it, and the shape of the `uipath.agent.autonomous` flow node that references it).
6	
7	## When to Use
8	
9	- Agent is tightly coupled to this specific flow
10	- No need for separate versioning, evaluation, or reuse across flows
11	- Fastest to set up — no separate agent project required
12	
13	## Standalone vs Inline
14	
15	| Aspect | Standalone | Inline |
16	|--------|-----------|--------|
17	| Location | Own project in solution | Subdirectory inside flow project, named by projectId (UUID) |
18	| Files | agent.json, entry-points.json, project.uiproj, flow-layout.json, evals/ | agent.json, flow-layout.json (`{}`), evals/eval-sets/ (empty), features/, resources/ |
19	| Lifecycle | Independent publish | Published with parent flow |
20	| Best for | Agent runs on its own or is referenced externally | Agent is a step within a flow |
21	
22	## Inline Agent Directory Structure
23	
24	An inline agent lives in a subdirectory named after its `projectId` (a UUID). It contains `agent.json`, an empty `flow-layout.json`, and empty scaffold directories:
25	
26	```
27	<FlowProject>/
28	├── <FlowName>.flow
29	├── project.uiproj              # Flow's project file
30	├── <projectId-uuid>/           # Inline agent subdirectory (UUID as folder name) ← inputs.source points here
31	│   ├── agent.json              # Agent definition (same schema as standalone — see ../../agent-definition.md)
32	│   ├── flow-layout.json        # Empty: {}
33	│   ├── evals/
34	│   │   └── eval-sets/          # Empty (no evaluators for inline agents)
35	│   ├── features/               # Empty
36	│   └── resources/              # Agent resources (tools, contexts, escalations)
37	└── ...
38	```
39	
40	### Key differences from standalone agent
41	
42	- **Folder name** is the agent's `projectId` UUID, not a human-readable name
43	- **`flow-layout.json`** is an empty JSON object `{}`
44	- **No `entry-points.json`** — the flow handles entry points
45	- **No `project.uiproj`** — governed by the parent flow project
46	- **`evals/`** contains only the `eval-sets/` subdirectory (empty) — no evaluators
47	- Has a root-level `guardrails: []` field
48	- No `metadata.targetRuntime`
49	
50	## Creating an Inline Agent
51	
52	### Option A: CLI command (recommended)
53	
54	```bash
55	uip agent init "<FlowProjectDir>" --inline-in-flow --output json
56	```
57	
58	This generates a UUID for the `projectId`, creates the subdirectory `<FlowProjectDir>/<uuid>/`, and scaffolds `agent.json`, `flow-layout.json`, and empty directories.
59	
60	> The scaffold sets `settings.model: "gpt-4o-2024-11-20"` (stale) and empty prompts. **Override the model** (`uip agent model list` → [model-selection-guide.md](../../model-selection-guide.md)) and write robust prompts ([prompting/agent-prompting-guide.md](../../prompting/agent-prompting-guide.md)) before validating.
61	
62	### Option B: Manual creation
63	
64	#### Step 1: Start with an existing flow project
65	
66	The flow project must already exist.
67	
68	#### Step 2: Generate a UUID and create the agent subdirectory
69	
70	Generate a unique UUID (e.g., `5029c8a8-799b-426a-803f-c4ec75255439`). Create a directory with that UUID as the name inside the flow project.
71	
72	#### Step 3: Create agent.json
73	
74	Same schema as a standalone agent (see [../../agent-definition.md](../../agent-definition.md)), with these conventions:
75	- `projectId` matches the folder name UUID
76	- `inputSchema.properties`: one `<triggerNodeId>__output__<global>` key per flow input — **mandatory**. See [§ Wiring Flow Inputs Into an Inline Agent](#wiring-flow-inputs-into-an-inline-agent-required).
77	- `messages[].content`: reference inputs as `{{input.<triggerNodeId>__output__<global>}}` (the `input.` form). Then run `uip agent refresh` to regenerate `contentTokens` from `content` — don't hand-author them. See [§ Wiring Flow Inputs Into an Inline Agent](#wiring-flow-inputs-into-an-inline-agent-required).
78	- `guardrails: []` at root level — can be populated with guardrail objects. See [../guardrails/guardrails.md](../guardrails/guardrails.md)
79	- No `metadata.targetRuntime` field
80	
81	Example:
82	```json
83	{
84	  "version": "1.1.0",
85	  "settings": {
86	    "model": "anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6",
87	    "maxTokens": 16384,
88	    "temperature": 0,
89	    "engine": "basic-v2",
90	    "maxIterations": 25,
91	    "mode": "standard"
92	  },
93	  "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": {} },
94	  "outputSchema": {
95	    "type": "object",
96	    "properties": {
97	      "content": { "type": "string", "description": "Output content" }
98	    }
99	  },
100	  "metadata": {
101	    "storageVersion": "50.0.0",
102	    "isConversational": false,
103	    "showProjectCreationExperience": false
104	  },
105	  "type": "lowCode",
106	  "guardrails": [],
107	  "messages": [
108	    { "role": "system", "content": "", "contentTokens": [] },
109	    { "role": "user", "content": "", "contentTokens": [] }
110	  ],
111	  "projectId": "5029c8a8-799b-426a-803f-c4ec75255439"
112	}
113	```
114	
115	#### Step 4: Create flow-layout.json
116	
117	```json
118	{}
119	```
120	
121	#### Step 5: Create empty directories
122	
123	```
124	evals/eval-sets/
125	features/
126	resources/
127	```

129	## Wiring Flow Inputs Into an Inline Agent (required)
130	
131	**The CLI does not derive the input wiring** — you author it; `refresh` only regenerates `contentTokens` from `content` (it does not fill `inputSchema` or `agentInputVariables`). `flow validate` *does* catch a prompt↔schema mismatch (a `{{input.K}}` that's malformed or names a key not in `inputSchema`), but **not** a missing/wrong node `agentInputVariables` binding — that delivery gap surfaces only at `flow debug`.
132	
133	This skill authors the **`agent.json` side** (flatten rule: `$vars.<trigger>.output.<var>` → `<trigger>__output__<var>`):
134	- `inputSchema.properties` — one `<trigger>__output__<var>` key per input (mandatory; binds the delivered `JobArguments` into the agent's `input`). Empty schema → the agent sees the literal `input.<key>` token even when the value arrived.
135	- `messages[].content` — reference each input as `{{input.<trigger>__output__<var>}}` (the `input.` form, **not** `$vars`), plus a real system prompt. `content` is the source of truth; run `uip agent refresh` to generate the matching `contentTokens` from it (don't hand-author them).
136	
137	```json
138	"inputSchema": { "properties": {
139	  "start__output__disputeSummary": { "type": "string", "description": "Bound from $vars.start.output.disputeSummary" }
140	} },
141	"messages": [{ "role": "user",
142	  "content": "Write a billing resolution email for this dispute:\n{{input.start__output__disputeSummary}}" }]
143	```
144	
145	The **flow side** — the trigger global and the node `agentInputVariables[]` binding (the only thing the converter turns into `JobArguments`) — is authored through the `uipath-maestro-flow` skill (Critical Rule 15). The full four-piece contract, the converter behavior, and the `content`↔`contentTokens` invariant + validator errors all live there: [inline-agent prompt-wiring guide § Wiring Flow Variables into Agent Prompts](../../../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/author/references/plugins/inline-agent/impl.md#wiring-flow-variables-into-agent-prompts).
146	
147	## Refresh and Validate Inline Agent
148	
149	```bash
150	uip agent refresh "<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>" --inline-in-flow --output json
151	uip agent validate "<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>" --inline-in-flow --output json
152	```
153	
154	`--inline-in-flow` skips the `entry-points.json` / `project.uiproj` checks. In inline mode `refresh` regenerates `messages[].contentTokens` (from `content`) and `bindings_v2.json` — **not** `entry-points.json` (standalone only). `validate` is read-only (it flags `contentTokens` drift but doesn't repair it — fix by re-running `refresh`).
155	
156	**Verify at `flow debug`, not after refresh:** `refresh` never fills `inputSchema` — it is non-empty only because you authored it (`DerivedFiles: 0` is normal and does **not** mean input is missing). The end-to-end check (run `uip maestro flow debug` and confirm the agent resolves the input rather than echoing the literal `input.<key>` token) is owned by the `uipath-maestro-flow` skill — see its [inline-agent guide § Debug](../../../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/author/references/plugins/inline-agent/impl.md#debug).
157	
158	For inline agents with external capabilities (tools, contexts, memory spaces, or escalations), pass `--bindings-target` to **`refresh`** after all flow graph edits:
159	
160	```bash
161	uip agent refresh "<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>" --inline-in-flow \
162	  --bindings-target "<FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json" --output json
163	```
164	
165	`--bindings-target` propagates the inline agent's bindings (process, connection, index, memorySpace, app, etc.) into the flow project's `bindings_v2.json`. This is required for `uip solution resources refresh` to discover the bindings and create solution-level resource files. Never hand-edit `bindings_v2.json`.
166	
167	> **Ordering constraint:** run the final `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow --bindings-target …` after all flow graph edits are complete. The `uipath-maestro-flow` skill owns direct `.flow` authoring for the inline-agent node, capability-resource nodes, and edges; refresh last so the generated bindings land in the flow project's `bindings_v2.json` before `uip solution resources refresh`. See the [Walkthrough](#walkthrough--end-to-end) for the correct sequence.

169	## Flow Wiring
170	
171	After creating the inline agent, the flow needs a `uipath.agent.autonomous` node whose `inputs.source` is the inline agent's `projectId` UUID, plus edges connecting it to the rest of the flow.
172	
173	**Hand off to the `uipath-maestro-flow` skill for the actual node and edge authoring.** Per Critical Rule 15, this skill does not invoke flow operations directly. Tell the user:
174	
175	> The inline agent has been scaffolded at `<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>/`. To wire it into the flow, use the `uipath-maestro-flow` skill — pass it `projectId = <uuid>` so it can add a `uipath.agent.autonomous` node with `inputs.source = <uuid>` and connect the input/success edges via direct `.flow` authoring. **After all flow graph edits are complete**, run `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow`, then `uip agent validate --inline-in-flow`; for inline agents with external capabilities, include `--bindings-target <FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json` on the refresh call.
176	
177	The node JSON shape that the flow skill must produce is documented in § Flow Node Structure below — keep it as a reference, not as a CLI walkthrough.
178	
179	## Inline-in-Flow Resource Paths
180	
181	Inline-agent resources — `tool`, `context`, `escalation` — share one path convention. Memory spaces are features, not `resources/` files; add them with `uip agent memory add ... --path <FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>` and see [../memory/memory.md](../memory/memory.md).
182	
183	**Path:** `<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>/resources/<RES_UUID>/resource.json`
184	
185	`<RES_UUID>` is a fresh UUID. It MUST match (a) the resource node's `inputs.source` in the flow and (b) the `id` field inside `resource.json`. The resource directory name is the UUID — never the human-readable resource name. Human-readable folder names are the standalone-agent convention; inline agents always use UUIDs.
186	
187	Resource body shape is identical to the standalone-agent docs — only the folder name differs:
188	- Tools (`process` / `agent` / `api` / `processOrchestration`): [../process/process.md](../process/process.md) § Subtypes and § Tool resource.json Shape. Discovery is identical (`uip solution resources list` + `uip solution resources get`); subtype is selected by the `type` field.
189	- Context index: [../context/index.md](../context/index.md) § Agent-Level Resource Shape.
190	- Escalation: [../escalation/escalation.md](../escalation/escalation.md) § Agent-Level Resource.
191	
192	### Tool-specific notes
193	
194	- **`location`**: Follows the same rule as standalone agents — set `"solution"` when the row from `uip solution resources list` has `Source: "Local"`, set `"external"` when `Source: "Remote"`. See [../process/process.md](../process/process.md) and [../../critical-rules/critical-rules.md](../../critical-rules/critical-rules.md) Rule 12.
195	- **`properties.folderPath`**: Must be the **literal folder path from discovery** (e.g., `"Shared/Sales"`) — do **not** leave it empty. An empty `folderPath` prevents `uip solution resources refresh` from resolving the tool at runtime.
196	- **`inputSchema.properties`**: Must include `"guardrails": { "type": "array" }` alongside the tool arguments — the runtime expects it.
197	- **All fields from the template in [../process/process.md](../process/process.md) are required** — especially `$resourceType: "tool"`, `guardrail`, `properties.processName`, `properties.exampleCalls`, `isEnabled`, and `argumentProperties`. A `resource.json` missing `$resourceType` will not be recognized by `uip agent validate` (the tool reports `"resources": 0`); `uip agent refresh` will then write an empty `bindings_v2.json`.
198	
199	## Flow Node Structure
200	
201	### Node type
202	
203	| Node type | Description |
204	|-----------|-------------|
205	| `uipath.agent.autonomous` | Autonomous reasoning agent embedded in the flow |
206	
207	### `.flow` node JSON
208	
209	```jsonc
210	{
211	  "id": "autonomousAgent1",
212	  "type": "uipath.agent.autonomous",
213	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
214	  "display": { "label": "Autonomous Agent" },
215	  "inputs": {
216	    "systemPrompt": "You are an agentic assistant.",
217	    "userPrompt": "What is the current date?",
218	    "source": "<projectId-uuid>",        // UUID linking to the inline agent directory
219	    "agentInputVariables": [],
220	    "agentOutputVariables": [
221	      { "id": "content", "type": "string" }
222	    ]
223	  },
224	  "outputs": {
225	    "output": {
226	      "type": "object",
227	      "description": "Agent response",
228	      "source": "=result.response",
229	      "var": "output"
230	    },
231	    "error": {
232	      "type": "object",
233	      "description": "Error information if the node fails",
234	      "source": "=Error",
235	      "var": "error"
236	    }
237	  }
238	}
239	```
240	
241	**Critical fields:**
242	- `inputs.source` — The inline agent's `projectId` UUID. Must match the subdirectory name and `agent.json.projectId` inside the flow project. The definition still declares `model.source: true`, but flow-core hoists that identity field onto `inputs.source` for the `uipath.agent.autonomous` node instance.
243	- `inputs.systemPrompt` / `inputs.userPrompt` — Current flow validation requires non-empty placeholders on the node. The canonical prompts still live in `agent.json.messages[]`.
244	- `definitions[]` — The `uipath.agent.autonomous` definition copied from the flow registry supplies `model.serviceType: "Orchestrator.StartInlineAgentJob"`, BPMN type, version, and context. Do not copy those fields into the node instance.
245	- No node instance `model` block — the inline-agent source lives at `inputs.source`.
246	
247	Resource nodes use the same `inputs.source` pattern as the autonomous agent — no instance `model` block. The `type` follows the per-kind patterns in § Resource nodes below — `uipath.agent.resource.tool.{process|agent|api|processorchestration}.<release-key>`, where `<release-key>` is the resource's release-key GUID returned by `uip solution resources list`:
248	
249	```jsonc
250	{
251	  "id": "agentTool1",
252	  "type": "uipath.agent.resource.tool.<kind>.<release-key>",
253	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
254	  "display": { "label": "<ToolName>" },
255	  "inputs": {
256	    "source": "<RES_UUID>"
257	  }
258	}
259	```
260	
261	The definition declares `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity field onto the node instance as `inputs.source` (same hoisting rule as `uipath.agent.autonomous`). The same shape applies to `uipath.agent.resource.escalation.*` and `uipath.agent.resource.context.*` nodes.
262	
263	### Handles
264	
265	| Handle | Position | Allowed connections |
266	|--------|----------|---------------------|
267	| `escalation` | top | `uipath.agent.resource.escalation.*` |
268	| `context` | bottom | `uipath.agent.resource.context.*` |
269	| `tool` | bottom | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.*` |
270	| `input` | left | Previous flow node |
271	| `success` | right | Next flow node |
272	| `error` | right | Error handler (when enabled) |
273	
274	### Resource nodes (tools, contexts, escalations)
275	
276	Resources are separate canvas nodes wired to the agent via artifact handle edges:
277	
278	```jsonc
279	// Edge connecting tool to agent:
280	// sourceNodeId: "autonomousAgent1", sourcePort: "tool"
281	// targetNodeId: "agentTool1", targetPort: "input"
282	```
283	
284	| Resource type | Node type pattern |
285	|--------------|-------------------|
286	| RPA process | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.process.<release-key>` |
287	| Agent-as-tool | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.agent.<release-key>` |
288	| API workflow | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.api.<release-key>` |
289	| Process Orchestration | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.processorchestration.<release-key>` |
290	| Built-in tool | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.builtin.<tool-name>` |
291	| IS connector | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.connector` |
292	| Semantic index | `uipath.agent.resource.context.index.<index-name>.<index-id>` |
293	| Escalation | `uipath.agent.resource.escalation.<variant>` (e.g. `.coded-action-app`; discover with `uip maestro flow registry search "escalation"`) |
294	| Memory space | `uipath.agent.resource.memory.*` canvas node, backed by `features/<FeatureName>/feature.json` from `uip agent memory` |
295	
296	`<release-key>` is the resource's release-key GUID from `uip solution resources list` (the row's `Key` field). The four process-tool kinds share the same registry-discovery flow and the same `resource.json` shape — only the prefix in front of `<release-key>` and the `type` field in `resource.json` differ. See [../process/process.md](../process/process.md) § Subtypes.

336	## What Happens at Pack Time
337	
338	`flow-workbench` extracts inline agents during `uip solution upload` / `uip solution pack`:
339	
340	1. Reads the inline agent directory referenced by `inputs.source` UUID
341	2. Collects connected resource nodes via artifact handles
342	3. Packages the `AgentDefinition` from the inline agent's `agent.json`
343	4. Writes into package:
344	
345	```
346	content/
347	├── process.bpmn
348	├── operate.json            # contentType: "Flow"
349	├── entry-points.json       # type: "processorchestration"
350	├── bindings_v2.json
351	└── agents/
352	    └── <agentProjectId>/
353	        ├── agent.json      # Extracted AgentDefinition
354	        └── .agent-builder/
355	            ├── agent.json  # Execution model
356	            └── bindings.json
357	```
358	
359	## Node Type Quick Reference
360	
361	```
362	uipath.agent.autonomous                                        ← Inline agent node
363	
364	uipath.agent.resource.tool.process.<release-key>               ← Tool: RPA process
365	uipath.agent.resource.tool.agent.<release-key>                 ← Tool: agent
366	uipath.agent.resource.tool.api.<release-key>                   ← Tool: API workflow

368	uipath.agent.resource.tool.connector                           ← Tool: IS connector

375	## BPMN Execution Engine Notes
376	
377	- **Inline agents**: `ServiceTask` with `serviceType: "Orchestrator.StartInlineAgentJob"`. The agent definition is read from the inline agent directory (`inputs.source` UUID) and executed in-process.
378	
379	The execution is asynchronous. The flow pauses at the agent node and resumes when the agent job completes.
380	
381	## Gotchas
382	
383	See [../../critical-rules/autonomous-critical-rules.md](../../critical-rules/autonomous-critical-rules.md) Critical Rule 1. The skill explicitly defers flow authoring to `uipath-maestro-flow` — it does not invoke that skill automatically ([../../critical-rules/critical-rules.md](../../critical-rules/critical-rules.md) Critical Rule 15).
384	
385	**Capability bindings must be propagated to the flow project's `bindings_v2.json`.** Only project-level bindings are scanned by `uip solution resources refresh`. Pass `--bindings-target <FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json` to `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow` — refresh is the command that writes the bindings. Without project-level propagation, Studio Web debug can fail because no solution-level resource file is created for the external capability.
386	
387	Run the final `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow --bindings-target …` as the **last step** before `uip solution resources refresh`, after all flow graph edits are complete. See the [Walkthrough](#walkthrough--end-to-end) for the correct sequence.

1	# Autonomous Agents Prompting Guide
2	
3	This is the prompting guide for low-code autonomous agents.
4	
5	"Coding-agent-centric" = the prompt makes the embedded agent behave like a disciplined tool-using agent: explicit tool-call criteria, stop conditions, structured output. Maps to the agent's `tool` artifact ports and `outputSchema`.
6	
7	## 1. System-prompt skeleton
8	
9	Copy this skeleton, fill every slot. Consistent structure → consistent runs. Put role/behavior here; data/task goes in the user message (§2).
10	
11	```text
12	You are <ROLE> for <DOMAIN>. <ONE-LINE PURPOSE>.
13	
14	Scope:
15	- In scope: <what the agent handles>
16	- Out of scope: <what to refuse or escalate>
17	
18	Tools:
19	- <toolName>: call when <explicit condition>. Do not call when <condition>.
20	- <toolName>: ...
21	Stop calling tools once <stop condition>; then produce the final answer.
22	
23	Output:
24	- Return a result conforming to the output schema. <field>: <how to fill it>.
25	- Never invent fields or values not grounded in the input or a tool result.
26	
27	Uncertainty:
28	- If <required input> is missing or ambiguous, <ask | set field to null | escalate> — do not guess.
29	- If you cannot complete the task, return <explicit failure shape>, not a fabricated answer.
30	```
31	
32	Slot rules:
33	
34	- **Role + scope** — name the role, bound it. An unbounded agent answers off-task prompts.
35	- **Tool-call criteria** — one trigger condition per tool, plus a stop condition. Without this the agent over-calls or loops to `maxIterations`.
36	- **Output contract** — state that output MUST match `outputSchema`; map each field. Without it the agent free-forms prose.
37	- **Grounding** — forbid values not traceable to input or tool output. Cuts hallucination.
38	- **Iteration budget** — for multi-tool tasks, note the agent has limited iterations (`maxIterations`, default 25) and should act, not deliberate.
39	
40	## 2. User-prompt anatomy
41	
42	The user message carries the task and the data — not the role.
43	
44	```text
45	<TASK INSTRUCTION>.
46	
47	<LABEL>: {{ $vars.<flowNodeId>.output.<field> }}
48	<LABEL>: {{ $vars.<flowNodeId>.output.<field> }}
49	
50	<EXPLICIT OUTPUT INSTRUCTION — e.g. "Return the category and a one-sentence reason.">
51	```
52	
53	Token form depends on context:
54	
55	- **Inline-in-flow agents** reference upstream flow nodes: `{{ $vars.<flowNodeId>.output[.<field>] }}`. See the [uipath-maestro-flow inline-agent prompt-wiring guide](../../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/author/references/plugins/inline-agent/impl.md#wiring-flow-variables-into-agent-prompts).
56	- **Standalone agents** reference declared inputs: `{{input.<field>}}`.
57	
58	Mirror every `{{ ... }}` in `contentTokens[]` per [agent-definition.md § contentTokens Construction](../agent-definition.md#contenttokens-construction).
59	
60	## 3. Grounding in wired data
61	
62	Reference inputs through tokens — never restate their literal contents in prose. The runtime injects the value; restating it duplicates tokens and risks drift if the upstream field changes. Tell the agent *what the field is*, not *what it contains*.
63	
64	## 4. Worked example — email triage
65	
66	Realistic inline-in-flow agent. Note the **structured `outputSchema`**, not a bare `content` blob.
67	
68	**Before (toy):**
69	
70	```json
71	"settings": { "model": "gpt-5.4" },
72	"outputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "content": { "type": "string" } } },
73	"messages": [
74	  { "role": "system", "content": "You are an assistant." },
75	  { "role": "user", "content": "Triage this email." }
76	]
77	```
78	
79	**After (robust):**
80	
81	```json
82	"settings": { "model": "anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6", "temperature": 0, "maxTokens": 4096, "maxIterations": 10 },
83	"outputSchema": {
84	  "type": "object",
85	  "properties": {
86	    "category": { "type": "string", "description": "One of: billing, technical, sales, other" },
87	    "priority": { "type": "string", "description": "low | medium | high | urgent" },
88	    "reason":   { "type": "string", "description": "One sentence justifying the category" },
89	    "needsHuman": { "type": "boolean", "description": "true if the email requires human review" }
90	  },
91	  "required": ["category", "priority", "needsHuman"]
92	}
93	```
94	
95	System prompt (filled skeleton):
96	
97	```text
98	You are a support-email triage classifier for a SaaS product. Classify each inbound email and flag those needing a human.
99	
100	Scope:
101	- In scope: categorizing the email and assessing priority.
102	- Out of scope: replying to the customer or taking any action — only classify.
103	
104	Output:
105	- Return a result conforming to the output schema. category MUST be one of billing, technical, sales, other. priority MUST be low, medium, high, or urgent.
106	- Set needsHuman=true for legal threats, churn risk, or anything outside the four categories.
107	- Never invent customer details not present in the email.
108	
109	Uncertainty:
110	- If the email is empty or unintelligible, set category="other", needsHuman=true, reason="unintelligible input".
111	```
112	
113	User prompt:
114	
115	```text
116	Classify the following email.
117	
118	From: {{ $vars.emailReceived1.output.from }}
119	Subject: {{ $vars.emailReceived1.output.subject }}
120	
121	{{ $vars.emailReceived1.output.body }}
122	
123	Return category, priority, a one-sentence reason, and needsHuman.
124	```
125	
126	## 5. Production checklist — adjacent `agent.json` quality fields
127	
128	A robust agent is more than its prompt. Each field: default, and when to change.
129	
130	| Field | Default | Change when |
131	|-------|---------|-------------|
132	| `outputSchema` | Scaffold gives a single `content` string | **Almost always** — define typed fields a downstream node can consume. Bare `content` forces brittle string-parsing. |
133	| `settings.temperature` | `0` | Keep `0` for extraction/classification/judgment. Raise only when output *variation* is wanted (drafting, brainstorming). |
134	| `settings.maxIterations` | `25` | Lower (≤5) for single-shot classification. Higher for multi-tool research loops. |
135	| `settings.maxTokens` | Scaffold value | Set ≤ the model's `MaxTokens` cap — see [model-selection-guide.md](../model-selection-guide.md#1-discover-primary-path). |
136	| `settings.model` | `gpt-5.4` | **Always override** — discover + select per [model-selection-guide.md](../model-selection-guide.md). |
137	| `guardrails` | `[]` | Add input/output policy enforcement (PII, content, escalation). See [capabilities/guardrails/guardrails.md](../capabilities/guardrails/guardrails.md). |
138	
139	## Anti-patterns
140	
141	- **Vague role** — "You are a helpful agentic assistant." Name the role and bound the scope.
142	- **No output contract** — agent free-forms prose; downstream nodes can't parse it.
143	- **Bare `content` output** — a single string where typed fields belong. Define `outputSchema`.
144	- **No tool-call criteria** — agent over-calls tools or loops to `maxIterations`.
145	- **Prompt-injection-prone passthrough** — pasting untrusted input into the system prompt. Keep untrusted data in the user message; keep instructions in the system message.
146	- **Ignoring `outputSchema`** — prompt that doesn't tell the agent to conform to the declared schema.
147	- **Cargo-culted `temperature`** — copying a nonzero temperature into a deterministic classification task.
